A background picture for a 2D narrative adventure game, made as a hand-carved three-block colour relief print: a woodcut and linocut in the manner of expressionist woodcut picture books of the early twentieth century. Technique: cut with V-gouges and U-gouges and a knife; the image is built from bold, coarse carved strokes and big solid shapes, never from drawn lines. Large areas of solid black ink; the light parts are cut away so the paper shows. Every form is described by carved strokes that follow it: the sky as long, tapering horizontal gouge strokes with stars as small cut crosses and dots, the low clouds as carved bands, the water as rows of short, curved carved wave strokes, the stone walls and the quay as chiselled blocks, the rocks as faceted chunks with wedge-shaped cuts, wood as long grain-like cuts. Shapes are simplified and chunky with strong silhouettes and slightly irregular hand-cut edges. Every carved stroke and every gap is at least 5 pixels wide; nothing is finer than that.

Printed with exactly three inks on cream paper: a black key block, a deep teal-blue block and a vermilion-orange block. Where the teal and the orange overlap they make a dark brown. Use only these colours: cream paper, black, deep teal-blue, vermilion-orange and the dark brown overlap. Every ink is completely flat and opaque: no gradients, no tints, no halftone dots, no shading, no airbrush, no glow, no thin pen lines, no fine hatching, no cross-hatching. Night is shown by large black areas and the teal ink; the light is the vermilion-orange band at the horizon, the lit window, the lantern glass and the lighthouse lamp, all as flat orange shapes. Clean, crisp ink edges, perfectly registered; no paper texture, no wood grain texture, no ink speckles, no stains, no frame, no border line (these printing effects are added later in the game). Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a watercolour, not a fine copper engraving, not a vector illustration with gradients, not a cartoon, not a postcard.

Composition for a wide game screen; the picture will later be cropped to a wide panoramic strip, so keep every important element between 17 % and 83 % of the picture height: above that only carved night sky, below that only plain quay paving. The viewpoint is close to the near quay, at the eye height of a small character: a character standing on the near quay will be about 25 % of the picture height tall, so everything on the near quay is large. The near quay paving is a band across the whole width from about 68 % of the picture height to the bottom edge; the character will walk along it at about 78 % of the height from the left edge to the middle, so keep the left two thirds of the near quay free and calm. In the near foreground at the right (72 to 98 % of the width), standing on the near quay: two barrels, each about a fifth of the picture height tall, a stack of crates and a coil of rope. The iron lantern on its wooden post stands at the back edge of the near quay at about 30 % of the width, the lantern itself against open sky at about 30 % of the picture height. The stone cottage stands further back on the left (0 to 22 % of the width), its roof and chimney fully in the picture, the chimney top at about 22 % of the picture height against open sky. The short wooden jetty with the two moored boats lies in the middle distance (35 to 65 % of the width), the horizon at about 52 % of the picture height. The lighthouse on its rocky headland stands in the distance at about 80 % of the width, its top at about 22 % of the picture height, its lamp against open sky. Wide areas of open carved sky above the jetty and of calm open water in front of it.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

The lighthouse lamp, the lantern glass and the lit window are only small flat orange shapes, without any beam, rays or glow around them; the chimney without smoke; no birds in the sky. Light beam, lantern rays, smoke and gulls are animated separately in the game.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, made as a hand-carved three-block colour relief print (woodcut and linocut), each figure about 400 pixels tall. The first reference image gives the exact layout, the exact size and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The first reference is a plain 3D render: take only the layout, the size and the poses from it, never its smooth shading or its plastic 3D look. The second reference image only shows the costume and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its colours or its three-view layout. The third reference image is the game background this character walks in: draw the character with exactly the same three inks, the same cream paper and the same coarse carved gouge strokes, so that it looks cut and printed from the same blocks.
